lines: In the middle's opening — yet the means: a powerful stand,
thoughts decaying, tightening, opening, and the rest, in many ways.
sanskrit_cite: madhyadhāmavikāse tu upāyo balavatsthitiḥ | vikalpakṣayasaṅkocavikāsādyā anekaśaḥ

lines: From thinking nothing, thoughts decay — so may it be;
from knowing-awareness, play-power, enamoured there, in being's field.
sanskrit_cite: akiñciccintanād eva vikalpānāṃ kṣayo bhavet | cidbodhād vilasacchaktī raktāsau bhāvamaṇḍale

lines: Fixed there, the bright flood sees the pure in nature;
power's tightening — fie, so say the brahma-teachers.
sanskrit_cite: tatrānuraktā divyaughaṃ paśyate vimalātmakam | śaktisaṅkocam etad dhi procyate brahmavādibhiḥ

lines: Point-rests at end and start — bindu, nāda — and grasps
of dread, fear, anger, loathing.
'Thus,' she said: goddess, middle's opening —
there the strong in days thus win supreme reward.
sanskrit_cite: ity etat kathitaṃ devi madhyadhāmavikāsakam | tatra śakto dinair evaṃ prapnoti parasampadam

lines: Who roams impressed with inner samādhi, pure-rayed —
by emission-power reflecting — again, and again.
sanskrit_cite: yo 'ntaḥsamādhisaṃskāraṃ bhramate vimalatviṣām | sa visargabalād eva vimṛśya ca punaḥ punaḥ

lines: In distraction even — his own form fully shines —
the yogi's, awareness-fixed, eternal-bliss-essenced.
sanskrit_cite: vyutthāne 'pi yatas tasya svarūpaṃ samprakāśate | yogino bodhaniṣṭhasya nityānandarasasya ca

lines: That — bliss-made-manifest, mantra-strong, full-I knowing —
so, of the inward-exulting devotee.
sanskrit_cite: tat prakāśānandamayī mantravīryopabṛṃhitā | pūṛnāhantācid ity antaḥsamullāsābhiyoginaḥ

lines: There — that sporting yogi, mantra-Lord-status stayed —
there strong, a lord, as he plays, power-swollen.
sanskrit_cite: tatrāsau vilasan yogī mantreśvarapade sthitaḥ | tatra śakto vibhur yadvat krīḍate śaktibṛṃhitaḥ

lines: Thus freedom — his, everywhere-going, world-Lord's, tasting all difference —
unbroken in the wonder-state.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ svatantratā tasya vyāpakasya jagadvibhoḥ | nānābhedajuṣaś citrapadasthitasyākhaṇḍitā
